what: Every error caught in the R(3,10) lane, by whom and how, from the control room’s log and notes: ours and the models’ alike, never a person’s. Errors inside the sealed box are one line each with a date and nothing of the method. A correction of a correction is one row, never counted as a finding.

rows.what: A note said the verified checker cake_lpr was built only for x86; its final release ships an ARMv8 build, which ran on the Mac.
A field of the global scout’s results held |J|, the touched part of a neighbourhood, under the name of |T| = |J| + 1; the claim was the same.
rows.outcome: the track was asked to name the field so

rows.what: Round 2 of the control room’s log was first stamped 02:15 UTC; it was written about 01:40.
The pilot’s pinned CNF generator was changed after it was pinned, and the pinned bytes were not on disk.
rows.outcome: the pinned bytes restored beside the changed file; listed as a gap

mattered.title: A pinned file changed after pinning
mattered.line: The pilot’s CNF generator was edited after its hash was pinned. The pinned bytes were restored beside it and the gap was listed.

rows.what: A first report said nothing was running; a second benchmark was running on four workers.
The run’s script hashed one of its files and then appended the end time to it, so one listed hash is of the file’s earlier state.
rows.outcome: listed; the file without its last line has the listed hash

rows.whose: the plan and the prior-art scout (an agent)
rows.caught_by: the reveal draft (an agent, reading our own files against each other)
rows.what: Two of our files said the Lean bridge rests on a native_decide axiom; the proof as checked uses none, only the three standard axioms. Both were written before the kernel proof.
rows.outcome: the result note is the record

rows.how: reading the statement against the record
rows.what: The sealed text adds that Exoo’s 39-vertex graph attains the bound. Our record shows only that a 39-vertex graph attains it; that it is Exoo’s rests on the two tracks’ checks.
rows.outcome: the page says “the bound 39 is attained”

rows.what: Our pre-registration says it was written about 17:35 UTC; its timestamp receipt was submitted at 17:22 UTC.
rows.outcome: listed; the receipt is the time

rows.what: Our plan still listed the verified checker as not run on C35; the result note has it accepting both proofs. One check time was also given as 0.6 s in three files and 0.31 s in the result.
rows.outcome: the result note is the record

rows.what: Our files disagree on who first stated C35: the brief, the round files and the sealed statement give three different splits between the two model tracks.
rows.outcome: open: the credit is mine to give

rows.what: A registration’s header said a draft’s hash was “in the block below”; it is in a separate file.
A brief gave the report’s author a wrong first name. The report and its Zenodo record name him Zhiyang Chen.

rows.how: building and reading by our own route
rows.what: A report called one Lean theorem “every independence clause at levels 3, 4 and full depth”: it is one theorem with the level idle, and no clause of the CNF is in that Lean.
rows.outcome: listed in the reading; no theorem changed

rows.what: An agent called leanchecker --help, which has no such flag and starts a full replay; stopped after about two minutes, nothing written. It happened again at 18:25 UTC.
rows.outcome: stopped; every later tool ran under a wrapper with limits

rows.what: The same slip as in production, this time in our script: it appended to a progress log after hashing it.
The first five replays exited 1 within a second: the tool started Lean from a path with no default toolchain.
rows.outcome: rerun with the toolchain first on the path; the failed logs kept

rows.what: A report cited a Lean line for the independence proof that holds another definition.
A note said three native runs passed; no log, script or binary of them is in its folder. The control room reproduced them.

mattered.title: Three runs with no files
mattered.line: A model’s note said three runs had passed; no log, script or binary was in its folder. The control room ran them again itself.

rows.what: A report’s list of what the production argument still needs was short by five items; its own note had two of them.
A report said a planted change was “caught at the first changed index”; the replay log holds no such control.
A step in a model’s proof was worded ambiguously; the step was valid.
A claim that rules were fixed before a test was backed only by local clocks.
A second claim of registration before the outcome was backed only by local clocks.
A check described as separate was the same track’s own, written three minutes later.
The rented machine of the all-rows byte check stood idle 20 minutes after the run ended, because a notice arrived late: about US$0.32.
rows.outcome: deleted; pods are now checked near their expected end

rows.what: Our time estimate for the running computation was too low.
rows.outcome: recorded as a deviation; I chose to let it run

rows.what: Audited files were edited in place: the originals were kept, but a hash manifest stopped checking.
rows.outcome: restored at the audited hashes (19:29 UTC)

rows.what: An earlier formula, carried into a new setting, failed there.
A report gave figures with no file behind them.
rows.outcome: the files were produced later (20:39 UTC)

rows.what: A safeguard claimed for a future test was not what its program checked.
rows.outcome: refused; rebuilt and certified by reading (22:06 UTC)

rows.what: A note said 39 native rows matched the ledger’s hashes; its log held the word SAME and no hashes.
rows.outcome: the track added the 39 hashes (19:12 UTC)

rows.how: the track’s reply, then the files
rows.what: We wrote that no theorem joins the CNF’s soundness proof (T1) to the other track’s closing theorem. Wrong: its bridge applies T1, and the closing theorem’s hypothesis is written with the same constants. It repeated a gap that file had closed.

mattered.title: A gap that was not there
mattered.line: We wrote that no theorem joined the two halves of the R(7) Lean chain. The Claude track showed the join; we withdrew the claim and filed an erratum.

rows.whose: a model session (by its content, the Astra track’s)
rows.what: A session of the other track wrote into two of the Claude track’s result notes, under that track’s heading; it happened again at 19:32 UTC.
rows.outcome: the blocks moved out verbatim to a dated file; a rule: each track writes only in its own folders

rows.what: Four phrases in a model’s report said more than its files.
Audited files were replaced in place again, and a hash list went stale.
rows.outcome: a rule: an audited file is never overwritten; a new version takes a new name

rows.what: A hash given in a message was taken before the file’s last write.
rows.outcome: checked against the file on disk

rows.what: A report said a fresh replay (leanchecker --fresh) had passed; its log had no such line. A transcript was filed later, without a time.
A test receipt shown as the track’s own was ours, read in place from our seal folder.
An agent ran two read-only commands on our seal folder and left one empty file.
Three hash suffixes were misprinted in our audit notes; the files were right.
Our first draft of a public status line named this private lane’s rented machine. The commit was refused before it was made.
rows.outcome: rewritten with the public lane only

rows.what: Programs sent a User-Agent naming the project to two public services from a private lane.
A machine presented as independent was a virtual machine on the same computer.
Two statements in a model’s note were refuted; one more had never been measured.

rows.caught_by: the Claude track, then an audit
rows.what: A reason given in one of our audit notes was wrong; its conclusion stood.

mattered.title: Our own wrong reason
mattered.line: Inside the sealed box: a reason given in one of our audit notes was wrong. Its conclusion stood, and an erratum was filed.

rows.what: A slip in one of our own notes was carried into a model’s text.

rows.caught_by: an outside review I pasted in
rows.what: The two seals’ Bitcoin receipts were still pending in our records, hours after a block could confirm them.

rows.how: rereading Chen’s repository before a note to him
rows.what: Our result note (in its sealed text too), our reveal draft and our first note to Chen called R(7) Chen’s open case. His own AI run had excluded it first, on 21 Nov at 16:50:52 UTC.
rows.outcome: our wording changed: a second computation of a case his run closed first; the sealed sentence is corrected beside it, in box 2

mattered.title: Chen’s run had closed R(7) first
mattered.line: Found by our own reread of his repository before writing to him. Our wording changed to “a second computation”, and a sentence of our sealed note is corrected beside it.

rows.what: A model’s cost estimate was not supported.
Three wording slips in a model’s report.
A model’s reading called a lower bound “Chen’s”; it is an unnumbered lemma in an idea-scout note of his run, not in his claims list.
rows.outcome: the page names it as the scout note’s

rows.what: We read a timestamp receipt only in part and “corrected” a registration’s time to a later one; the whole receipt proves the earlier time.

rows.caught_by: the reveal day’s prior-art re-check (an agent)
rows.what: Our prior-art scout of 21 Nov missed a public note (andrey-kokoev/marici, dated 9 Nov) that had posed the induced-C35 question and left it not excluded.
rows.outcome: the page cites it beside the theorem

rows.caught_by: the reveal package (an agent), reading Chen’s history
rows.what: Our 04:02 note put the label “cert (custom trace)” of Chen’s C-004 at his round 1; it arrived in round 2, at 17:49:01 UTC.
rows.outcome: corrected in the reveal’s source and here

rows.whose: the second program (the Astra track’s code)
rows.how: a second program’s full run, joined with ours by our own code
rows.what: An independent second program, run over every input of the sealed computation, disagreed with ours on a small number of inputs; until each was decided, no input it touched counted as closed. Found 07:31 UTC.
rows.outcome: resolved at 08:01 UTC; no verdict changes
rows.resolution: Resolved: the second program was the one in error (it omitted two conditions of a screen both programs implement); ours was right, and every input the disagreement touched was decided anyway by our tests and our second method. No verdict changes. The second program is being corrected and will be compared again over every input when the sealed run ends.
